q: A capacitor is used as an electric circuit component to store electrical energy.
e: True. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. A capacitor is used as an electric circuit component to store electrical energy.

q: The capacitor was originally known as a resistor.
e: False. The right claim is this: The capacitor was originally known as a condenser. Condenser is the old name; the modern word is capacitor. The printed line wrongly says the capacitor was originally known as a resistor.

q: A capacitor is an electrical device that stores electrical energy in the form of an electric field.
e: True. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Device that stores electrical energy in the form of an electric field.

q: A capacitor consists of three conductors separated by a small distance.
e: False. The right claim is this: A capacitor consists of two conductors separated by a small distance. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it. The printed line wrongly says a capacitor consists of three conductors separated by a small distance.

q: An insulator is inserted between the conductors of a capacitor.
e: True. The plates must conduct so charge can spread; the gap must insulate or the field collapses. An insulator is inserted between the conductors of a capacitor.

q: Film capacitors are the ones that use plastic film as the dielectric medium.
e: True. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. Film capacitors are the ones that use plastic film as the dielectric medium.

q: Film capacitors are available with working voltages up to 500 V.
e: False. The right claim is this: Film capacitors are available in working voltages up to 1500 V. Film capacitors use plastic film, take high voltage, and are not polarized. The printed line wrongly says film capacitors are available with working voltages up to 500 V.

q: Ceramic capacitors are the ones that use ceramic as the dielectric material.
e: True. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Ceramic capacitors are the ones that use ceramic as the dielectric material.

q: Ceramic capacitors are mainly used for low stability performances with high losses.
e: False. The right claim is this: Ceramic capacitors are mainly used for high stability performances with low losses. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. The printed line wrongly says ceramic capacitors are mainly used for low stability performances with high losses.

q: Electrolytic capacitors are the ones that use the oxide layer as the dielectric material.
e: True. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. Electrolytic capacitors are the ones that use the oxide layer as the dielectric material.

q: There are mainly two types of electrolytic capacitors; tantalum and copper.
e: False. The right claim is this: There are mainly two types of electrolytic capacitors; tantalum and aluminum. Electrolytics use an oxide film, pack large C, and the polarity mark must be respected. The printed line wrongly says there are mainly two types of electrolytic capacitors; tantalum and copper.

q: Electrolytic capacitors are available with working voltages of up to approximately 500 V.
e: True. Electrolytics use an oxide film, pack large C, and the polarity mark must be respected. The value 500 V is the figure this statement is using.

q: The failure of electrolytic capacitors is completely safe and never hazardous.
e: False. The right claim is this: The failure of electrolytic capacitors can be hazardous, resulting in an explosion or fire. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. The printed line wrongly says the failure of electrolytic capacitors is completely safe and never hazardous.

q: Electrolytic capacitors are used for filtering and smoothing rectified alternating voltage.
e: True. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points. Electrolytic capacitors are used for filtering and smoothing rectified alternating voltage.

q: Variable capacitors mostly use water as the dielectric medium.
e: False. The right claim is this: Variable capacitors mostly use air as the dielectric medium. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. The printed line wrongly says variable capacitors mostly use water as the dielectric medium.

q: The capacitance of a variable capacitor can be mechanically adjusted.
e: True. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. The capacitance of a variable capacitor can be mechanically adjusted.

q: Variable capacitors are mostly used in DC circuits especially for high frequency.
e: False. The right claim is this: Variable capacitors are mostly used in AC circuits especially for high frequency, high power and low loss. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current. The printed line wrongly says variable capacitors are mostly used in DC circuits especially for high frequency.

q: A supercapacitor is also called an ultracapacitor.
e: True. An ultracapacitor packs huge C into a small volume for rapid charge and discharge. A supercapacitor is also called an ultracapacitor.

q: A supercapacitor has a capacitance value much lower than other capacitors.
e: False. The right claim is this: A supercapacitor (SC), also called an ultracapacitor, is a high-capacity capacitor with a capacitance value much higher than other capacitors. An ultracapacitor packs huge C into a small volume for rapid charge and discharge. The printed line wrongly says a supercapacitor has a capacitance value much lower than other capacitors.

q: A supercapacitor bridges the gap between electrolytic capacitors and rechargeable batteries.
e: True. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. A supercapacitor bridges the gap between electrolytic capacitors and rechargeable batteries.

q: A supercapacitor typically stores 10 to 100 times more energy than electrolytic capacitors.
e: True. An ultracapacitor packs huge C into a small volume for rapid charge and discharge. A supercapacitor typically stores 10 to 100 times more energy than electrolytic capacitors.

q: A supercapacitor can accept and deliver charge much slower than batteries.
e: False. The right claim is this: A supercapacitor can accept and deliver charge much faster than batteries. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates. The printed line wrongly says a supercapacitor can accept and deliver charge much slower than batteries.

q: Film capacitors and ceramic capacitors are polarized capacitors.
e: False. The right claim is this: Film capacitors and ceramic capacitors are non-polarized capacitors. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. The printed line wrongly says film capacitors and ceramic capacitors are polarized capacitors.

q: Capacitors are used for blocking AC current after getting fully charged but allow the DC current to pass through it.
e: False. The right claim is this: Capacitors are used for blocking DC current after getting fully charged but allow the AC current to pass through it. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. The printed line wrongly says capacitors are used for blocking AC current after getting fully charged but allow the DC current to pass through it.

q: Capacitors can be used in a time-dependent circuit such as a timer circuit.
e: True. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Capacitors can be used in a time-dependent circuit such as a timer circuit.
